text: Our general mindset is in two months, there's going to be a better model and it's going to blow away whatever the current set of limitations are. And we say this to developers too.
speaker: Kevin Weil
context: Lenny asks Kevin about what it's like working at the center of the AI revolution at OpenAI. Kevin explains their philosophy of 'model maximalism' - the idea that instead of building extensive workarounds for current model limitations, they focus on the fact that AI models improve dramatically every few months. He's advising both internal teams and external developers to push the boundaries of what's currently possible, knowing that upcoming model improvements will make products that barely work today perform exceptionally well in the near future.
text_ko: 저희 일반적인 생각은 두 달만 지나면 더 나은 모델(model)이 나와서 현재의 제약들을 완전히 뛰어넘을 거라는 거예요. 이 얘기는 개발자들(developers)한테도 똑같이 해요.
text_zh: 我们普遍的想法是：两个月内会有更好的模型 (model) 出来，能把现在这些限制都彻底打破。我们也会这么跟开发者 (developers) 说。
text_es: Tendemos a pensar que en dos meses saldrá un modelo (model) mejor que dejará obsoletas las limitaciones actuales. Se lo decimos también a los desarrolladores (developers).
key_sentence: there's going to be a better model and it's going to blow away whatever the current set of limitations are.
original_text: Our general mindset is in two months, there's going to be a better model and it's going to blow away whatever the current set of limitations are. And we say this to developers too. If you're building and the product that you're building is kind of right on the edge of the capabilities of the models, keep going because you're doing something right. Give it another couple months and the models are going to be great, and suddenly the product that you have that just barely worked is really going to sing.

vocabulary.definition: A particular way of thinking or a mental attitude that influences how one perceives and responds to situations.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a growth mindset encourages innovation and adaptability, essential for navigating challenges and seizing opportunities.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'mindset' generally refers to a person's attitude, it can imply a fixed or flexible approach depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: Restrictions or constraints that hinder progress or performance in a particular context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, understanding limitations is crucial for setting realistic goals and developing strategies to overcome obstacles.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a negative connotation, suggesting barriers that need to be addressed or mitigated.

vocabulary.definition: A representation or framework that illustrates a concept, system, or process, often used for analysis or simulation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In startups, a business model outlines how a company creates, delivers, and captures value, guiding strategic decisions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can refer to both theoretical frameworks and practical applications, so context is important to clarify its use.

text: Everywhere I've ever worked before this, you kind of know what technology you're building on, but that's not true at all with AI.
speaker: Kevin Weil
context: Lenny asks what's most different about working at OpenAI compared to Kevin's previous roles at traditional tech companies like Twitter, Instagram, and Facebook. Kevin explains that unlike conventional software development where the underlying technology stack remains relatively stable, AI development is fundamentally different because the core capabilities of the models evolve rapidly. This constant advancement in AI capabilities requires product teams to continuously rethink their approach and strategies.
text_ko: 여태까지 일해본 곳들에서는 보통 어떤 기술을 기반으로 하는지 대충 알 수 있었어요. 그런데 인공지능(AI)은 전혀 그렇지 않아요.
text_zh: 在我以前工作的那些地方，通常能大概看出你们是搭在什么技术上的，但在人工智能（AI）这块完全不是这么回事。
text_es: En todos los trabajos anteriores más o menos sabes en qué tecnología te apoyas, pero con la inteligencia artificial (AI) eso no es así en absoluto.
key_sentence: you kind of know what technology you're building on, but that's not true at all with AI.
original_text: Everywhere I've ever worked before this, you kind of know what technology you're building on, but that's not true at all with AI. Every two months, computers can do something they've never been able to do before and you need to completely think differently about what you're doing.

vocabulary.definition: The application of scientific knowledge for practical purposes, especially in industry. It encompasses tools, systems, and methods that enhance productivity and efficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech settings, technology is often a key driver of innovation, enabling companies to improve processes, create new products, and gain competitive advantages.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'technology' typically refers to modern innovations, it can also imply a broader range of tools and systems, so context is important to clarify its scope.

vocabulary.definition: To develop or expand upon an existing idea, foundation, or framework, often to enhance or innovate further.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and technology, 'building on' refers to leveraging existing technologies or concepts to create new products or services, fostering growth and evolution.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a collaborative or cumulative approach to development, emphasizing the importance of prior work while also indicating potential for further advancement.

text: keep going, because you're doing something right... the models are going to be great, and suddenly the product that you have that just barely worked is really going to sing.
speaker: Kevin Weil
context: Lenny asks about OpenAI's product philosophy and how they approach building products when the underlying AI technology is constantly improving. Kevin is explaining their 'model maximalism' approach - rather than building extensive workarounds for current AI limitations, they advise developers to build products that push current model capabilities to their limits. His point is that products struggling with today's models will excel as the models rapidly improve over the coming months.
text_ko: 계속 밀고 가세요. 지금 하시는 게 맞아요. 모델(models)이 훨씬 좋아질 거고, 어느 순간 겨우 돌아가던 프로덕트(product)가 진짜 빛을 발할 거예요.
text_zh: 坚持下去，你现在做对了。模型(models)会越来越强，那个现在还只是勉强能用的产品，突然就会大放异彩。
text_es: Sigue así, porque estás haciendo algo bien... los modelos (models) van a ser excelentes, y de repente ese producto que apenas funcionaba va a empezar a brillar.
key_sentence: Keep going if your product barely worked; models will soon really sing.
original_text: If you're building and the product that you're building is right on the edge of the capabilities of the models, keep going, because you're doing something right because you give it another couple months and the models are going to be great, and suddenly the product that you have that just barely worked is really going to sing.

text: I think you're definitely going to live in a world where you have researchers built into every product team. And I don't even mean just at foundation model companies because I think the future...
speaker: Kevin Weil
context: Lenny asks Kevin about how product teams might change in the future as AI becomes more prevalent. Kevin predicts that product teams across all companies, not just AI companies, will need to include researchers or machine learning engineers. He explains that the future will involve extensive use of fine-tuned models - AI models customized for specific use cases rather than using generic models. This will require teams to have the expertise to adapt and optimize models for their particular product needs.
text_ko: 앞으로는 분명 모든 제품 팀(product team)에 연구자들이 정규 멤버로 들어가는 세상에서 살게 될 거예요. 그리고 제가 그걸 파운데이션 모델 회사들(foundation model companies)에만 해당된다고 말하는 것도 아니에요. 제 생각엔 미래에는...
text_zh: 我觉得将来你肯定会生活在一个每个产品团队里都配备研究员（researchers）的世界里。我并不是只说那些做基础模型的公司（foundation model companies），因为我觉得未来……
text_es: Creo que, sin duda, vamos a vivir en un mundo en el que cada equipo de producto va a tener investigadores integrados. Y no me refiero solo a las empresas de modelos fundacionales (foundation model companies), porque creo que el futuro...
key_sentence: you're definitely going to live in a world where you have researchers built into every product team.
original_text: I think you're definitely going to live in a world where you have researchers built into every product team. And I don't even mean just at foundation model companies because I think the future... Actually, frankly one thing that I'm sort of surprised about about our industry in general is that there's not a greater use of fine-tuned models.

vocabulary.definition: A product team is a group of professionals responsible for the development, design, and management of a specific product or product line within an organization.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product teams often include roles such as product managers, designers, and engineers who collaborate to bring a product from concept to market.
vocabulary.nuance: The term emphasizes collaboration and cross-functional expertise, distinguishing it from other teams that may focus solely on marketing or sales.

vocabulary.definition: A foundation model refers to a large-scale machine learning model that serves as a base for further customization and fine-tuning for specific applications or tasks.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, foundation models are often utilized in artificial intelligence to streamline the development of applications, enabling companies to leverage advanced capabilities without building models from scratch.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a robust and versatile model that can be adapted for various uses, highlighting its foundational role in AI development.

vocabulary.definition: Researchers are individuals who conduct systematic investigations to establish facts, gather data, and develop new knowledge in a specific field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of tech and startups, researchers play a critical role in innovation, often working on product development, market analysis, and technological advancements.
vocabulary.nuance: The term carries a connotation of rigor and academic inquiry, and is typically used to refer to individuals with advanced expertise in their field.

text: if you teach your kids to be curious, to be independent, to be self-confident, you teach them how to think... those are going to be skills that are going to be important in any configuration of the future.
speaker: Kevin Weil
context: Lenny asks Kevin, who has three children, what skills he's encouraging his kids to learn to prepare for an AI-dominated future. A community member jokingly worried that by 2036, kids might need to compete for spots in roofing or plumbing programs as AI takes over other jobs. Kevin responds with a thoughtful perspective that instead of trying to predict specific career paths, parents should focus on developing fundamental human capabilities that will remain valuable regardless of how technology evolves.
text_ko: 자녀에게 호기심을 갖게 하고, 자립심과 자신감을 길러주면 사고하는 법을 가르치는 거예요. 그런 능력들은 미래가 어떻게 변하든 어디서나 중요해요.
text_zh: 如果你培养孩子的好奇心、独立性和自信，实际上就是在教他们怎么思考——这些能力在任何未来场景下都会很重要。
text_es: Si enseñas a tus hijos a ser curiosos, independientes y seguros de sí mismos, les estás enseñando a pensar por sí mismos. Esas habilidades serán clave en cualquier escenario futuro.
key_sentence: if you teach your kids to be curious, to be independent, to be self-confident, you teach them how to think
original_text: I think if you teach your kids to be curious, to be independent, to be self-confident, you teach them how to think, I don't know what the future holds, but I think that those are going to be skills that are going to be important in any configuration of the future.

vocabulary.definition: Not relying on others for support or guidance; capable of self-sufficiency.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being independent often refers to individuals or teams that can make decisions and take actions without needing approval from higher authorities, fostering innovation and agility.
vocabulary.nuance: While independence is generally positive, it can imply a lack of collaboration if taken to an extreme.

vocabulary.definition: Having a strong belief in one's own abilities and judgment; assured in oneself.
vocabulary.businessContext: Self-confidence is crucial in business environments, as it enables individuals to present ideas assertively, negotiate effectively, and lead teams with conviction.
vocabulary.nuance: Self-confidence is often viewed positively, but excessive self-confidence can lead to overestimating one's abilities and making poor decisions.

vocabulary.definition: The arrangement or setup of components in a system or structure; the way in which something is organized.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, configuration often refers to the setup of software systems, networks, or organizational structures to optimize performance and functionality.
vocabulary.nuance: Configuration can imply a level of customization or adaptability, and is often used in contexts where specific arrangements are necessary for efficiency.

vocabulary.definition: The abilities or expertise that enable an individual to perform tasks effectively; often acquired through training or experience.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, skills are critical for workforce development, as they determine an employee's capability to contribute to projects and drive organizational success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'skills' can encompass both hard skills (technical abilities) and soft skills (interpersonal abilities), and is often used in discussions about employee training and development.

text: It fundamentally disappoints me that this doesn't exist in the world today because the world would be a better place if we'd been able to ship that product. We tried to launch a new blockchain. It was a basket of currencies originally.
speaker: Kevin Weil
context: Lenny asks Kevin about Libra, the cryptocurrency project he worked on at Facebook that ultimately failed. Kevin explains that Libra was designed to solve real problems like expensive international remittances, where people pay 20% fees to send money to family in other countries. The project aimed to enable instant, free money transfers through WhatsApp and Messenger using a new blockchain and basket of currencies. Kevin expresses genuine disappointment that this product never launched because he believes it would have made the world better by solving these costly, inefficient payment problems.
text_ko: 솔직히 이게 아직 세상에 없는 게 너무 안타까워요. 그 제품을 출시할 수만 있었더라면 세상이 더 나아졌을 거예요. 저희는 새 블록체인(blockchain)을 출시하려고 했어요. 원래는 여러 통화를 묶은 통화 바스켓(basket of currencies)이었어요.
text_zh: 让我很失望的是，这东西现在还不存在——要是我们能把那款产品真的推出来，世界会更好一些。我们当时试着推出一个新的区块链(blockchain)，最初打算把它做成一个货币篮子(basket of currencies)。
text_es: Me decepciona profundamente que esto no exista hoy en día; el mundo sería un lugar mejor si hubiéramos podido sacar ese producto al mercado. Intentamos lanzar una nueva cadena de bloques (blockchain). Al principio era una cesta de divisas (basket of currencies).
key_sentence: It fundamentally disappoints me that we couldn't ship that product; the world needs it.
original_text: It fundamentally disappoints me that this doesn't exist in the world today because the world would be a better place if we'd been able to ship that product. We tried to launch a new blockchain. It was a basket of currencies originally. It was integration into WhatsApp and Messenger. I would be able to send you 50 cents in WhatsApp for free. It should exist.

vocabulary.definition: In a basic and essential way; at the core or root of something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, 'fundamentally' is often used to emphasize the core principles or values that underpin a strategy or decision.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of depth and importance, suggesting that the issue at hand is not just superficial but intrinsic to the matter.

vocabulary.definition: To introduce a new product, service, or initiative to the market or public.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, 'launch' refers to the critical phase when a company makes its product available to consumers, often accompanied by marketing efforts.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies a sense of excitement and anticipation, and is often associated with significant planning and investment.
